claims.quote: Suppose presently we find it is possible to quicken that decay?
claims.description: Radioactive decay might be artificially accelerated to release atomic energy.

claims.quote: not only should we have a source of power so potent that a man might carry in his hand the energy to light a city for a year, fight a fleet of battleships, or drive one of our giant liners across the Atlantic
claims.description: Controlled atomic energy would give a handheld power source able to light a city, power warships or liners.

claims.quote: Every scrap of solid matter in the world would become an available reservoir of concentrated force.
claims.description: Induced disintegration of all elements would turn any matter into an energy source.

claims.quote: Then that perpetual struggle for existence, that perpetual struggle to live on the bare surplus of Nature’s energies will cease to be the lot of Man.
claims.description: Abundant atomic energy would end humanity's struggle for subsistence.

claims.quote: I see the desert continents transformed, the poles no longer wildernesses of ice, the whole world once more Eden.
claims.description: Cheap energy would transform deserts and the polar regions into fertile land.

claims.quote: I see the power of man reach out among the stars....
claims.description: Atomic energy would enable humanity to travel to the stars.

claims.quote: the problem of inducing radio-activity in the heavier elements and so tapping the internal energy of atoms, was solved by a wonderful combination of induction, intuition, and luck by Holsten so soon as the year 1933.
claims.description: Induced radioactivity and release of atomic energy is achieved in the laboratory in 1933.

claims.quote: What chiefly impressed the journalists of 1933 was the production of gold from bismuth and the realisation albeit upon unprofitable lines of the alchemist’s dreams
claims.description: Artificial transmutation of bismuth into gold via induced radioactivity.

claims.quote: this must eventually change war, transit, lighting, building, and every sort of manufacture, even agriculture, every material human concern
claims.description: Atomic energy will transform war, transport, lighting, building, manufacturing and agriculture.

claims.quote: Holsten, before he died, was destined to see atomic energy dominating every other source of power
claims.description: Atomic power becomes the dominant energy source within one scientist's lifetime.

claims.quote: It was in 1953 that the first Holsten-Roberts engine brought induced radio-activity into the sphere of industrial production, and its first general use was to replace the steam-engine in electrical generating stations.
claims.description: Atomic engines replace steam engines in power stations.

claims.quote: Allowing for lubrication the Dass-Tata engine, once it was started cost a penny to run thirty-seven miles, and added only nine and quarter pounds to the weight of the carriage it drove.
claims.description: A compact atomic engine powers automobiles at extremely low running cost.

claims.quote: men found themselves possessed of an instrument of flight that could hover or ascend or descend vertically and gently as well as rush wildly through the air.
claims.description: Atomic-powered aeroplanes with helicopter-style vertical takeoff and hover become widespread.

claims.quote: atomic smelting was embarked upon so eagerly as to lead to a number of disastrous explosions due to inexperienced handling of the new power
claims.description: Atomic smelting adopted in industry, causing accidental explosions.

claims.quote: one of the recoverable waste products was gold
claims.description: Atomic engines produce gold as a by-product, depreciating its value.

claims.quote: The coal mines were manifestly doomed to closure at no very distant date, the vast amount of capital invested in oil was becoming unsaleable
claims.description: Cheap atomic power makes coal mining and oil investment obsolete, causing mass unemployment and financial panic.

claims.quote: In the year 1955 the suicide rate for the United States of America quadrupled any previous record.
claims.description: Economic dislocation from atomic energy causes a surge of suicides and violent crime.

claims.quote: The Dass-Tata people were indeed making a strenuous attempt to secure a world monopoly in atomic engineering.
claims.description: Patent wars over atomic engines as companies try to monopolize the technology.
